neighbours.label: the token ' insulin' / '-ulin' (the hormone insulin, in any language); its counterpart glucagon also fires, other hormones and 'blood sugar' much less
fire: After a sugary snack the body responds by releasing insulin into the blood.
Her doctor adjusted the dose of insulin she takes each morning.
Muscle cells become more sensitive to insulin after regular exercise.
The pump delivers a steady trickle of insulin through a thin tube.
Banting and Best first isolated insulin in a Toronto laboratory.
Type 1 patients cannot make their own insulin and depend on injections.
Between meals the liver responds to glucagon by releasing stored glucose.
Chronic overeating can blunt the response of fat cells to insulin.
quiet: After a frightening noise the body responds by releasing adrenaline into the blood.
Her doctor adjusted the dose of thyroxine she takes each morning.
Muscle cells become more sensitive to testosterone after regular exercise.
The pump delivers a steady trickle of morphine through a thin tube.
Fleming first noticed penicillin in a London laboratory.
Some patients cannot make enough thyroid hormone and depend on tablets.
Between meals the liver slowly releases its stored glucose.
Chronic overeating can raise blood sugar and strain the heart.

notes: Card: ' insulin' x18 and 'ulin' x9 of the top 32, plus Japanese and Russian spellings. Probes: insulin 0.55-0.72, glucagon 0.56; leptin 0.21, cortisol 0.17, blood sugar 0.16, estrogen 0.12. One fire sentence uses glucagon on purpose, as the label says.
